source_text: Processimus itaque iam ad exempla, uti reuoluamus utilitatis efficacia potestates istius officii, quod etiam iratum deum homini reconciliat. deliquerat Israel in aquatione apud Maspha congregatus a Samuele, sed ita statim delictum ieiunio diluit, ut periculum proelii simul fugerit. cum maxime Samuel offerebat holocaustum (in nullo magis procuratam audimus dei clementiam quam in abstinentia populi) et allophyli proelio admouebant, ibidem dominus intonuit uoce magna super allophylos, et confusi sunt et corruerunt in conspectu Israelis, et processerunt uiri Israel ex Maspha et persecuti sunt allophylos et usque Bethor ceciderunt, pastos impasti, armatos inermes. hae erunt uires ieiunantium deo. caelum pro eiusmodi militat. habes formam praesidii etiam spiritalibus bellis necessariam. perinde cum rex Assyriorum Sennacherib compluribus iam ciuitatibus captis Israeli per Rapsacen blasphemias et minas intentaret, nihil aliud illum a proposito in Aethiopias auertit. dehinc quid aliud centum et octoginta quatuor milia de exercitu eius per angelum absumpsit quam Ezechiae regis humiliatio? siquidem duritia hostis adnuntiata uestem scidit, saccum induit eodemque habitu seniores sacerdotum ad deum per Esaiam adire iussit utique ieiunio preces prosequente. neque enim cibi tempus in periculo nec saturitatis cultus in sacco. semper inedia maeroris sequela est sicut laetitia accessio saginae. per hanc maeroris sequelam et inediam etiam ciuitas illa peccatrix Niniue de exitio praedicato liberatur. satis enim paenitentia scelerum commendauerat ieiunium triduo functam, etiam pecudibus enectis, quibus iratus deus non erat. Sodoma quoque et Gomorra euasissent, si ieiunassent. hoc remedium agnoscit et Achab. cum illi post transgressionem et idololatriam et necem Nabuthae propter uineam interempti a Iezabel exprobrasset Helias: qualiter occidisti et hereditatem possedisti: in loco quo sanguinem Nabuthae canes delinxerant, tuum quoque delinguent, destituit semetipsum et saccum carni suae imposuit et ieiunauit et dormiuit in sacco. et tunc sermo domini ad Heliam: uidisti ut reueritus sit Achab a facie mea: pro eo, quod reueritus est, non superducam laesuram in diebus ipsius, sed in diebus filii eius superducam eam, qui non erat ieiunaturus. ita ieiunium in deum reuerentiae opus est, per quod Anna quoque ambiens uxor Helcanae retro sterilis impetrauit facile a deo inanem cibo uentrem filio implere et quidem propheta. sed non modo naturae mutationem aut periculorum auersionem aut delictorum obliterationem, uerum etiam sacramentorum agnitionem ieiunia de deo merebuntur. aspice Danielis exemplum. circa somnium regis Babylonis omnes turbantur sophistae, negant ultra de praestantia humana posse cognosci. solus Daniel deo fidens et sciens, quid ad demerendam dei gratiam faceret, spatium tridui postulat, cum sua fraternitate ieiunat, atque ita orationibus commendatis et ordinem et significationem somnii per omnia instruitur, tyranni sophistis parcitur, deus glorificatur, Daniel honoratur, non minorem dei gratiam et postea quoque relaturus anno primo regis Darii, cum ex recogitatu praedicatorum temporum ab Hieremia dedit faciem suam deo in ieiuniis et sacco et cinere. nam et angelus missus ad eum hanc statim professus est causam diuinae dignationis: ueni, inquit, demonstrare tibi, quatenus miserabilis es, ieiunando scilicet. si deo miserabilis, leonibus in lacu fuerat horribilis, ubi quidem illi sex diebus ieiunanti prandium angelus procurauit.
thought_title: Fasting as remedy: examples from Israel's history
orientation: Tertullian is now marshaling Old Testament examples to show that fasting reconciles an angry God to man, beginning with Israel at Mizpah under Samuel.
pass_a_gloss: We have proceeded therefore now to the examples, so that we may roll back the effective powers of the usefulness of this duty, which also reconciles an angry God to man. Israel had sinned in the water-drawing at Mizpah, gathered by Samuel, but so immediately it washed away the sin by fasting, that it fled at the same time the danger of battle. When especially Samuel was offering a burnt offering (in nothing more do we hear the mercy of God procured than in the abstinence of the people) and the foreigners were moving to battle, in that same place the Lord thundered with a great voice over the foreigners, and they were thrown into confusion and fell in the sight of Israel, and the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the foreigners and cut them down as far as Beth-horon, the fed [by] the unfed, the armed [by] the unarmed. These will be the powers of those fasting for God. Heaven fights for such men. You have a form of protection necessary also for spiritual wars. Likewise when the king of the Assyrians Sennacherib, with very many cities already captured, was directing blasphemies and threats against Israel through Rabshakeh, nothing else turned him away from his purpose into Ethiopia. Then what else consumed one hundred and eighty-four thousand of his army through an angel than the self-humbling of King Hezekiah? Since indeed when the hardness of the enemy was announced he tore his garment, put on sackcloth, and in the same dress ordered the elders of the priests to approach God through Isaiah, with fasting certainly accompanying the prayers. For neither is it a time for food in danger, nor is the attire of fullness in sackcloth. Always fasting is the companion of grief, just as joy is the addition of overindulgence. Through this companion of grief and fasting also that sinful city Nineveh is freed from the destruction that had been proclaimed. For sufficiently had repentance of crimes commended the fasting, having performed it for three days, with even the cattle killed, with which God was not angry. Sodom also and Gomorrah would have escaped, if they had fasted. This remedy Achab also recognizes. When Elijah had reproached him after the transgression and idolatry and the murder of Naboth because of the vineyard, [Naboth] having been killed by Jezebel: 'How have you killed and possessed the inheritance? In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, they will lick yours too,' he set himself aside and put sackcloth on his flesh and fasted and slept in sackcloth. And then the word of the Lord [came] to Elijah: 'Have you seen that Achab has shown reverence before my face? Because he has shown reverence, I will not bring harm in his days, but in the days of his son I will bring it, who was not going to fast.' Thus fasting is a work of reverence toward God, through which also Hannah, the wife of Elkanah, going around formerly barren, easily obtained from God to fill her womb empty of food with a son, and indeed a prophet. But not only change of nature or turning away of dangers or blotting out of sins, but also recognition of mysteries will fasts merit from God. Look at the example of Daniel. Around the dream of the king of Babylon all the wise men are disturbed, they deny that it can be known further by human excellence. Daniel alone, trusting in God and knowing what to do to earn God's favor, asks for a space of three days, fasts with his brotherhood, and so with prayers commended he is instructed in both the order and the meaning of the dream through all things, the wise men of the tyrant are spared, God is glorified, Daniel is honored, [he] about to report not less of God's favor also afterwards in the first year of King Darius, when from reconsidering the times proclaimed by Jeremiah he gave his face to God in fasts and sackcloth and ashes. For also an angel sent to him immediately declared this cause of divine regard: 'I have come,' he said, 'to show you, since you are pitiable, by fasting of course.' If pitiable to God, he had been terrible to the lions in the pit, where indeed for him fasting for six days an angel procured a meal.

pass_b_english: We have now reached the examples, so let us review the effective powers of this duty's usefulness, which also reconciles an angry God to man. Israel had sinned at the watering place, gathered at Mizpah by Samuel, but so immediately washed away the sin by fasting that the danger of battle fled at the same time. While Samuel was offering the burnt offering—we hear of God's mercy being secured in nothing more than in the people's self-control—and the Philistines were moving into battle, the Lord thundered with a great voice over the Philistines, and they were thrown into confusion and fell before Israel, and the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines and struck them down as far as Beth-horon: the hungry cutting down the well-fed, the unarmed the armed. These will be the strengths of those who fast for God. Heaven fights for such people. You have the form of protection necessary even for spiritual wars.

Likewise, when Sennacherib king of the Assyrians, after many cities had already been captured, was directing blasphemies and threats against Israel through Rabshakeh, nothing else diverted him from his purpose toward Ethiopia. Then what else consumed 184,000 of his army through an angel but King Hezekiah's self-humbling? For when the enemy's harshness was announced, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and in the same dress ordered the elders of the priests to approach God through Isaiah, with fasting certainly accompanying the prayers. For there is no time for food in danger, nor is overindulgence the dress of sackcloth. Fasting is always the companion of grief, just as joy is the addition of overindulgence.

Through this companion of grief and fasting, that sinful city Nineveh was also freed from the destruction that had been proclaimed. For repentance had sufficiently commended the fasting of three days, even with the animals made to fast, with whom God was not angry. Sodom and Gomorrah would also have escaped if they had fasted.

Ahab also recognizes this remedy. When Elijah had reproached him after the transgression and idolatry and the murder of Naboth—killed by Jezebel for the vineyard—saying, 'How you have killed and taken possession! In the place where dogs licked Naboth's blood, they will also lick yours,' he set himself aside and put sackcloth on his flesh and fasted and slept in sackcloth. And then the word of the Lord came to Elijah: 'Have you seen how Ahab has shown reverence before my face? Because he has shown reverence, I will not bring disaster in his days, but in his son's days I will bring it'—the son who was not going to fast. So fasting is a work of reverence toward God, through which Hannah also, the wife of Elkanah, previously barren, easily obtained from God to fill her womb empty of food with a son, and indeed a prophet.

But not only changes of nature or the averting of dangers or the blotting out of sins, but also the recognition of sacred mysteries will fasts merit from God. Look at Daniel's example. Concerning the dream of the king of Babylon, all the wise men were troubled; they said it could no longer be known by human excellence. Daniel alone, trusting in God and knowing what to do to earn God's grace, asks for a space of three days, fasts with his companions, and so, with prayers commended, is instructed in the order and meaning of the dream in every detail. The tyrant's wise men are spared, God is glorified, Daniel is honored—and he was going to receive no less grace from God afterward, in the first year of King Darius, when from reconsidering the times proclaimed by Jeremiah he set his face toward God in fasts and sackcloth and ashes. For the angel sent to him immediately declared this as the cause of the divine favor: 'I have come,' he said, 'to show you, since you are pitiable'—by fasting, of course. If he was pitiable to God, he had been terrifying to the lions in the den, where indeed an angel procured a meal for him after six days of fasting.
